chapter: England, Paris and memories of Kansas City and Harlem
title: The Lascelles party and the 91st Psalm
summary: At a party given by the Queen's cousin, a black GI told her to read the 91st Psalm; she read all of them and began to pray.

story.theme_name: Church, faith and religion in a musician's life
story.community_name: Church, faith and jazz: the sacred and the secular

blocks.x: Yes, but what really happened that got me on to

praying was before I left England the Queen's cousin Lascelles follows jazz and he gave a party. I must have looked disturbed because there was one other black person, a GI. He says, "You seem like you're disturbed. My grandmother always said to read the 91st Psalm." I've never been able to drink at one time over two drinks without really getting high, so I thought he said read all the Psalms so I went home and started reading them all. Seemed like that just turned me around and started me to praying.
Just coming out of you now. Was this before you left England?
Then when you got to Paris, how did this develop?
